title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.37631v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. How these different kinds of knowledge are learned as pretraining progresses remains unclear. Recent point-in-time models trained on web snapshots from different years provide a way to probe how knowledge prevalence varies over time. Using these models, we propose a temporal variability score (TVS), defined as the coefficient of variation of an item's negative log-likelihood across models. A higher score suggests that the knowledge may be less consistently represented across years of web text. We evaluate six benchmarks covering diverse topics using six models from multiple open-source model families. We find that low- and high-TVS items are learned similarly early in training, but high-TVS items improve faster later on. At the end of the pretraining run, high-TVS items outperform low-TVS items in 34 of 36 model-bench

translated_title: 预训练过程中什么在提升？利用时点模型追踪知识获取
translated_abstract: 在跨越多年收集的网络语料库上预训练的语言模型既学习通用知识，也学习领域特定知识。随着预训练的进行，这些不同种类的知识是如何被习得的仍不清楚。最近在不同年份网络快照上训练的时点模型提供了一种探究知识流行度如何随时间变化的方法。利用这些模型，我们提出了时间变异性分数（TVS），定义为某个项目在各模型间负对数似然的变异系数。较高的分数表明该知识可能在多年网络文本中的表现不够一致。我们使用来自多个开源模型家族的六个模型评估了涵盖不同主题的六个基准。我们发现低TVS和高TVS项目在训练早期以相似的方式被学习，但高TVS项目在后期提升更快。在预训练运行结束时，高TVS项目在36个模型-基准组合中的34个中优于低TVS项目。
tldr: 该论文提出时间变异性分数（TVS）来衡量知识在不同年份网络文本中的一致性，发现高变异性知识在预训练早期与低变异性知识的学习速度相似，但在后期提升更快。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a temporal variability score (TVS) to measure how consistently knowledge is represented across years of web text, finding that high-variability knowledge is learned at similar rates early in pretraining but improves faster in later stages.
